title: Batch 10 Revelation geographic and visionary methodology
notes: Project-authored method: historical places may be mapped with confidence labels; visionary geography is never assigned ordinary terrestrial coordinates. Literary sequence is not equated with physical travel.
verificationNote: Project-authored curation methodology; no external source verification claim is implied.

title: Revelation — canonical text
notes: Canonical textual references only; the repository’s Bible-text licensing remains governed separately.

title: Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World
author: Richard J. A. Talbert, ed.
notes: Used as a general reference for Roman-period places and provincial geography.

title: The Seven Churches in their Asia Minor urban setting — curated archaeological bibliography
notes: Project synthesis drawing on site archaeology and standard historical geography; does not assert that Revelation’s metaphors have one-to-one archaeological explanations.

title: The Letters to the Seven Churches of Asia in Their Local Setting
author: Colin J. Hemer
notes: Influential contextual study; individual local-background proposals are treated as proposals rather than automatic explanations.

title: Revelation: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary
author: Craig R. Koester
notes: Anchor Yale Bible commentary used for literary, historical, and interpretive context.

title: Revelation 1–22
author: David E. Aune
notes: Word Biblical Commentary volumes used for historical-literary context and discussion of disputed identifications.

title: Twice Neokoros: Ephesus, Asia and the Cult of the Flavian Imperial Family
author: Steven J. Friesen
notes: Used for imperial-cult context; the project does not reduce Revelation to a single empire-cult explanatory model.

title: Pergamum archaeological and monumental context — project bibliography
notes: Used for the acropolis, Great Altar, sanctuaries, and urban setting. “Satan’s throne” is not archaeologically identified.

title: Archaeological Exploration of Sardis — project reference
notes: Used for the securely identified city and its archaeological landscape; later remains are not backdated to Revelation without qualification.

title: Cave of the Apocalypse and Monastery of Saint John — reception-history reference
notes: Used only for later Christian tradition on Patmos, not as first-century proof.

title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5.30.3
author: Irenaeus of Lyons
notes: Important early testimony often used for a Domitianic dating tradition; its wording and interpretation are discussed in scholarship.

title: Domitian and the Roman imperial context — project bibliography
notes: Used for reign dates and broad imperial setting. Revelation itself never names Domitian.

title: Genesis–Revelation canonical motif integration
notes: Project-authored thematic navigation connecting repeated biblical images without asserting direct historical geography between visionary scenes.
